title: The Permutation-Sign (Zolotarev) Route to Quadratic Reciprocity
content:
Zolotarev's lemma (1872) proves quadratic reciprocity through permutation signs instead of Gauss sums. For an odd prime $p$ and $a$ coprime to $p$, the map $\pi_a : x \mapsto a\cdot x$ permutes the nonzero residues $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times$, and Zolotarev's lemma asserts
$$\left(\tfrac{a}{p}\right) = \operatorname{sign}(\pi_a).$$
Reciprocity follows by computing the sign of one 'grid transpose' permutation two ways. This entry formalizes **Milestone 1**: the group-theoretic engine showing that multiplication by a generator is a single cycle whose sign is computable.
mathContext: The genuinely-new building block (isolated in session S9) is the *producer* lemma `isCycle_mulLeft_of_generator`, confirmed ABSENT from Mathlib at the repo pin v4.26.0 (mathlib rev 2df2f01). Mathlib supplies the *consumers* — `Equiv.Perm.IsCycle.sign` and `IsCycle.orderOf` — but not the constructor that mulLeft by a generator yields a cycle. Everything else (Euler's criterion `legendreSym.eq_pow`, the `sign` MonoidHom, `map_zpow`) is pinned wiring. Numerical certificates verify_zolotarev.py (the identity $(a/p)=\operatorname{sign}(\pi_a)$ for odd primes $3\le p<80$) and verify_m1_cycle_lemma.py (the IsCycle obligations for 45 odd primes) support the formalization build-free.

title: isCycle_mulLeft_of_generator — The Lemma Mathlib Lacks
content: In a finite group $G$ with $|G| \ge 2$ generated by $g$, left-multiplication $\operatorname{mulLeft} g : x \mapsto g\cdot x$ is a single cycle. The proof discharges the `IsCycle` constructor with base point $x = 1$: (i) $\operatorname{mulLeft} g$ moves $1$ to $g$, and $g \ne 1$ because $g$ generates a group of order $\ge 2$; (ii) every $y$ is on the cycle of $1$, since $y \in \langle g\rangle$ gives $i$ with $g^i = y$, and $(\operatorname{mulLeft} g)^i$ applied to $1$ equals $g^i \cdot 1 = y$.
mathContext: The key wiring $(\operatorname{mulLeft} g)^i = \operatorname{mulLeft}(g^i)$ has no direct Mathlib lemma (`Equiv.mulLeft_zpow`/`mulLeft_pow` confirmed absent at rev 2df2f01). It is obtained from `map_zpow` applied to the inline monoid hom $a \mapsto \operatorname{Equiv.mulLeft} a : G \to^* \operatorname{Perm} G$, bundled directly rather than naming a nonexistent lemma. This is the reusable, Mathlib-gap-filling core of the whole Zolotarev route.

title: sign_mulLeft_generator — The Sign is −1
content: For a finite group of even order generated by $g$, $\operatorname{sign}(\operatorname{mulLeft} g) = -1$. Because $g \ne 1$, $\operatorname{mulLeft} g$ has no fixed points, so its support is all of $G$. By `IsCycle.sign`, $\operatorname{sign} = -(-1)^{|G|}$, and since $|G|$ is even, $(-1)^{|G|} = 1$, giving $-1$.
mathContext: For the units group $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times$ the order is $p-1$, which is even for every odd prime $p$, so on a primitive root the Zolotarev sign is always $-1$. The evenness hypothesis is precisely what makes a full-length cycle an odd permutation.

title: sign_mulLeft_eq_neg_one_zpow — The Zolotarev Sign Computation
content: For $a = g^k$ with $g$ a generator of an even-order finite group, $\operatorname{sign}(\operatorname{mulLeft} a) = (-1)^k$. The proof factors $\operatorname{mulLeft}(g^k) = (\operatorname{mulLeft} g)^k$ (the inline $G \to^* \operatorname{Perm} G$ hom + `map_zpow`), then uses that `sign` is a `MonoidHom` (so it commutes with `zpow`) together with $\operatorname{sign}(\operatorname{mulLeft} g) = -1$.
mathContext: This is the full Zolotarev *sign computation* in discrete-log form. Combined with Euler's criterion $\left(\tfrac{a}{p}\right) = (-1)^k$ (where $k$ is the discrete log of $a$ to a primitive root) it yields Zolotarev's lemma $\left(\tfrac{a}{p}\right) = \operatorname{sign}(\operatorname{mulLeft} a)$ on $(\mathbb{Z}/p)^\times$. That Euler-criterion tie and the field/units sign bridge remain prose in knowledge.md (numerically certified) and are the immediate next milestone — the headline identity is NOT yet machine-checked, so the open question is not resolved.
prerequisites: Euler's criterion for the Legendre symbol
